paragraphs: Children in care in Midlothian are looked after by Midlothian Council's own fostering service, shown above alongside the independent services that take enquiries from the area, from Dalkeith and Bonnyrigg to Penicuik, Loanhead and Gorebridge. In May 2026 the council launched a campaign, Could You Be Part of Their Story?, to mark Foster Care Fortnight, with posters in libraries, leisure centres and GP surgeries across the county.

The council looks for carers for children aged 0 to 18 and offers temporary care, which can last weeks, months or until the end of childhood, permanent care, specialist care for children with higher needs, and planned respite. Its recruitment strategy has said it wants to place children with carers who live in Midlothian, and it has asked in particular for carers for sibling groups, teenagers and children with complex needs.

You need a spare bedroom so a child has privacy; a flat is fine, and renters should check with their landlord. Single people and couples can apply, with or without children, there is no age bar if you are fit enough. Respite carers do not have to be available full time, and many carers keep working.

Becoming a carer starts with a home visit and an enquiry report, followed by preparation groups and a home study over a few months, then a fostering panel. Each fostering family has its own social worker, a training programme, support groups and events through the year, and the council's 2026 campaign mentions paid annual leave as well as fees and allowances. Council carers are paid as self-employed, with the amount depending on the type of care, plus an allowance for the child's costs. From April 2026 the Scottish Recommended Allowance, the national minimum for a child's costs, is £177.68 a week for ages 0 to 4, £206.71 for 5 to 15 and £283.35 for 16 and 17; any carer fee is paid on top.
Contact the recruitment team on 0131 271 3615, and see our Edinburgh, East Lothian and Scotland pages for nearby services.
